title: TTL can delete a refreshed DATETIME row when global time_zone changes between scan and delete

payload.p_check: scan and delete carry the same expiration epoch
payload.q_claim: the delete-time predicate has the same DATETIME meaning as the scan predicate
payload.fast_path: each statement independently resets to current global time_zone and evaluates FROM_UNIXTIME(epoch)
payload.missing_dimension: the epoch token is stable but its DATETIME interpretation context is not
payload.c3_oracle: row is non-expired under scan context, then actual TTL worker silently deletes it and reports successful completion
controls: same worker schedule without time-zone change preserves the refreshed row
historical #41043 pre-job time-zone-change scenario is green on current source
source_anchors: docs/design/2022-11-17-ttl-table.md delete recheck and time-zone safety contract

history_dedup.reason: #41043 changes time zone before job start; current control is green. This target changes context between scan and delete inside one job and violates refreshed-row protection.

provenance.source: TiDB 13282a8bd06b plus test-only scheduling failpoint on testbed 8220955

name: Scan and irreversible recheck must preserve semantic context

payload.contract: A later safety recheck must preserve every semantic context component needed to interpret the token carried from the scan phase.
search_shape: scan or candidate phase carries a compact token
later phase rebuilds a safety predicate
admission_gate: mutate only that context between phases
prove current state is safe under original context
require an irreversible C3 oracle and a no-mutation control
payload.stop_rule: after one actual-worker RED and context-stable GREEN, do not enumerate offsets or batch sizes

name: TTL DATETIME scan and delete use one stable cutoff meaning

payload.p_check: scan selected a handle under DATETIME < FROM_UNIXTIME(E) in context C0
payload.q_claim: delete recheck uses the same wall-clock cutoff meaning
payload.fault: change global time_zone from UTC to +08 between scan and delete
payload.red: row refreshed beyond C0 cutoff is deleted and job completes
green_controls: no time-zone change preserves refreshed row

name: TTL delete must preserve a row refreshed beyond the scan cutoff

provenance.source: actual TTL worker matrix on testbed 8220955

name: Pause TTL after scan handoff and before delete context reset

payload.action: dynamic pause; update selected row and change global time_zone; release
altitude_controls: same pause and row update without time-zone change
invalid_if: scan has not materialized the handle
row is still expired under the original scan context
oracle checks generated SQL without actual worker completion

lessons.selector_worked: stable token did not imply stable predicate meaning across independently reset sessions
lessons.method_upgrade: handoff proofs must inventory semantic context owners, not only carried values

rationale: scan and delete share an epoch token but independently reload its interpretation context
the oracle proves the row is current under scan semantics and observes silent deletion
the pause isolates the scan-to-delete context handoff
